text: 果壳中的国王
en: The King in the Nutshell

text: 虽然许多人都在批判信息茧房，但这种看法低估了群众，而且没有确实的证据来证明人们真的被信息茧房所困（调查结果其实与人们设想的相反）。
en: Although many people criticise the information cocoon, this view underestimates the masses, and there is no solid evidence to prove that people are really trapped by information cocoons (survey results are actually the opposite of what people imagine).

text: 问题在于，既然如此之多的人对它进行批判，那为什么事情无法被改变呢？
en: The problem is: since so many people criticise it, why can't things be changed?

text: 因为终究，这仍是文化与习性的疾病。
en: Because ultimately, this is still a disease of culture and habit.

text: 无论我们把问题归结为历史终结，还是技术算法，都仅仅是一种客观化的进程。
en: Whether we attribute the problem to the end of history or to technical algorithms, it is merely a process of objectification.

text: 对异化的批判，既神话了技术，也神话了人，从而忽略了两者之间互相交叠、褶皱与干涉的作用，并提供了一种理性的幻觉。
en: Criticism of alienation both mythologises technology and mythologises people, thereby ignoring the overlapping, folding and interfering effects between the two, and providing a rational illusion.

text: 解释与批判现在都只是在褶皱当中激起的微小波澜：对技术的批判现在服务于人，但人本身又是被技术重构的现象，这便导致人们的讨论通常都只是重言式。
en: Explanation and criticism are now only small ripples stirred up within the folds: criticism of technology now serves people, but people themselves are phenomena reconstructed by technology, which leads people's discussions to usually be mere tautologies.

text: 一个简单的图示常常被无数人重复——难道不是构成了茧房本身？
en: A simple diagram repeated by countless people — does it not itself constitute a cocoon?

text: 所以在这里我们发现，恰恰是对信息茧房的批判主导了公众意识和思想——让他们对信息与权力保持迷信，从而在不自知当中陷入所谓的茧房。
en: So here we discover that it is precisely criticism of the information cocoon that dominates public consciousness and thought — making them superstitious about information and power, and thus unknowingly falling into the so-called cocoon.

text: 文化与习性只是在其中不断地自我加强。
en: Culture and habit only continuously strengthen themselves within it.

text: 所以左派的批评意味着什么？
en: So what does leftist criticism mean?

text: 贬低群众是为了形成所谓理性的权威，而高估群众则主要是因为要为人的需求寻找一个历史进程，使公众服从他们的解释，从而让他们产生人推动历史的幻觉。
en: Belittling the masses is to form so-called rational authority, while overestimating the masses is mainly to find a historical process for human needs, making the public obey their explanations, thereby giving them the illusion that people drive history.

text: 这样一来，便形成了一种庸俗的技术官吏阶层。
en: This in turn forms a vulgar class of technocrats.

text: 然而，技术带来的问题是，双重链接（正如德勒兹在《千高原》中指出的）。
en: However, the problem brought by technology is double articulation (as Deleuze pointed out in A Thousand Plateaus).

text: 就好比一个铁匠挥舞铁锤敲击铁砧，经历了一个碎裂的过程——由关节的撞击引起；另一方面，他也因此获得了一种人的新形式所特有的关节（链接），专门为劳作而设。
en: It is like a blacksmith swinging a hammer to strike an anvil, undergoing a process of fragmentation — caused by the impact of joints; on the other hand, he also thereby obtains a new form of human joints (articulations) specific to labour.

text: 一面是碎裂的分子化过程，另一面是克分子的沉积过程。
en: On one side is a fragmenting molecular process; on the other side is a depositing process of molar aggregates.

text: 其实这正是结构主义的方法。
en: This is actually the structuralist method.

text: 首先它把原始形式弄碎，然后再通过劳作的总体化机制，生产的配置与超编码，重新使之结构化（能指链的构建），于是一种有机体或国家的治理便形成了。
en: First it shatters the original form, and then through the totalising mechanism of labour, the configuration of production and overcoding, it restructures it (the construction of the signifier chain), and thus an organism or state governance is formed.

text: 这同样是网络用户体验如何被安排的。
en: This is also how the network user experience is arranged.

text: 它导致结构之中的用户产生新的迷信，就如同哈姆雷特，果壳中的国王：人人都有一种中心的幻觉，以及对权力的狂热；人人都想操控一切，像水军那样。
en: It leads users within the structure to develop new superstitions, just like Hamlet, the king in the nutshell: everyone has an illusion of centrality, and a fanaticism for power; everyone wants to control everything, like paid posters.

text: 人人都成了审判官和殖民者，疯狂地掠夺土地。
en: Everyone has become a judge and a coloniser, madly plundering land.

text: 但恰恰因为如此，一种信息茧房的幻影产生了。
en: But precisely because of this, a phantom of the information cocoon is produced.

text: 果壳中的国王并非对外界一无所知，但是他需要果壳来成为王；他疯狂地需要群众，以便在群众当中构筑边缘与中心的等级。
en: The king in the nutshell is not ignorant of the outside world, but he needs the nutshell to become king; he madly needs the masses, in order to construct hierarchies of margin and centre among the masses.

text: 虽然王的位置只有一个，根本没有办法被任何人占据，但是人们只要通过对普遍性的宣称——在自己的果壳中占据群众的权威——自居为群众发号施令，同时又排斥其它群众，便可产生果壳之王。
en: Although there is only one king's position, which cannot be occupied by anyone at all, people only need to claim universality — occupying the authority of the masses in their own nutshell — to order the masses around as if they were the masses, while excluding other masses, and a nutshell king can be produced.

text: 所以信息茧房的本质是什么呢？
en: So what is the essence of the information cocoon?

text: 其实是一套权力机制导致的愚昧。
en: It is actually ignorance caused by a set of power mechanisms.

text: 并不是墙规定了意识，而是意识的自我规定塑造了墙。
en: It is not the wall that determines consciousness, but consciousness's self-determination that shapes the wall.

text: 它是一种幻觉，却被人们用来自我说服——通过虚伪的批判，他们不断地以理性自居，不过却是为了占据王的位置。
en: It is an illusion, yet people use it to persuade themselves — through hypocritical criticism, they constantly pose as rational, but only in order to occupy the king's position.

text: 在此，他们只要服从与流量经济的规则，服从于理性，便可成为一个主体——但其实只是乌合之众。
en: Here, they only need to obey the rules of the traffic economy and obey rationality to become a subject — but in fact they are just a mob.

text: 在质疑解放激情的过程中展示“我思”，在聒噪中寻求“我在”，在美颜摄像头和调音设备中成为网红，在大多数的名义下发号施令。
en: Displaying 'I think' in the process of questioning liberating passions, seeking 'I am' in the noise, becoming influencers with beauty cameras and audio-tuning equipment, giving orders in the name of the majority.

text: 正所谓“水浅王八多”，信息茧房因池中之物的肤浅而显得格外强大。
en: As the saying goes, 'shallow water breeds many turtles' — the information cocoon appears particularly powerful because of the shallowness of the things in the pond.

text: 正因为毒蟾蜍的鸣叫盖过了百灵鸟的歌唱，所以信息茧房开始突兀地展示自身。
en: Precisely because the croaking of poisonous toads has drowned out the singing of larks, the information cocoon begins to conspicuously display itself.

text: 正因为对中心与等级的执着，果壳之王们聚集在一个又一个信息热点、一个又一个洼地当中，争吵不休的同时对边缘采取排斥和忽略的态度，所以信息茧房又成了它们用来庸人自扰的问题。
en: Precisely because of the obsession with centre and hierarchy, the nutshell kings gather in one information hotspot after another, in one lowland after another, quarrelling endlessly while adopting an attitude of exclusion and neglect towards the margins, so the information cocoon has become a problem they use to trouble themselves with.

text: 果壳之王，当然还是最在意果壳。
en: The nutshell king, of course, cares most about the nutshell.

text: 信息社会矛盾的地方在于，你发现的信息茧房这一问题，并且意识到它的危害性，极力想要避免它，却发现怎么也避免不了。
en: The contradictory aspect of the information society is that you discover the problem of the information cocoon, realise its harmfulness, and desperately want to avoid it, yet find you cannot avoid it no matter what.

text: 一个比较极端的方式：不上网，并且在生活中，对于你接触到的一切信息，持怀疑审慎的态度，辩证地对待。
en: A more extreme way: don't go online, and in life, maintain a sceptical and cautious attitude towards all information you come into contact with, and treat it dialectically.

text: 但我并不推荐这种方式，因为大多数人做不到。
en: But I do not recommend this way, because most people cannot do it.

text: 每个人每天即使不看微信微博这些高噪音密集App，也能通过互联网接触到其他千万条信息。
en: Even if each person does not look at high-noise, dense apps like WeChat and Weibo every day, they can still come into contact with tens of millions of other pieces of information through the internet.

text: 即使你不带手机出门，走在大街上，各路广告营销商都带有目的地呈现在你眼前，诱惑你买买买。
en: Even if you go out without your phone, walking on the street, all kinds of advertising marketers present themselves before your eyes with purpose, tempting you to buy, buy, buy.

text: 信息无处不在。
en: Information is everywhere.

text: 但我们大致可以把它分为两类：有用的和无用的。
en: But we can roughly divide it into two categories: useful and useless.

text: 有用的信息，应该是围绕你自身活动任务为主的信息，尽量主动获取他们。
en: Useful information should be information centred on your own activities and tasks; try to actively obtain it.

text: 你可以从朋友口中得知，也可以通过搜索引擎获取。
en: You can learn it from friends' mouths, or obtain it through search engines.

text: 比如你是一个python开发工程师，你首要接触的，是你的项目，你的相关领域的探索。
en: For example, if you are a Python development engineer, what you first come into contact with is your project and exploration in your related field.

text: 这个时候，你需要关注的，就是尽量在程序员的圈子里找到有价值的帮助信息。
en: At this time, what you need to focus on is finding valuable help information within the programmer community as much as possible.

text: 无用的信息，这可能是我们平常接触更多的。
en: Useless information is probably what we come into contact with more in ordinary times.

text: 微信里的群聊，微博知乎的热榜，朋友圈无关痛痒的推广，大多数和我们无关。
en: Group chats in WeChat, hot lists on Weibo and Zhihu, irrelevant promotions in Moments — most of them have nothing to do with us.

text: 而媒体和商家正在尽全力诱导我们去关注这些。
en: And media and businesses are doing their utmost to induce us to pay attention to these.

text: 面对这些无用的信息，意识到生活中那些事情对你才是最重要的，不断提醒自己，什么才是最重要的，然后你会下意识地尽可能去忽略无关信息，而把精力和心思放在重要的事情上。
en: Faced with this useless information, realise what things in life are most important to you, constantly remind yourself what is most important, and then you will subconsciously try to ignore irrelevant information as much as possible, and put your energy and thought into important things.

text: 比如阅读，和朋友谈心，学习一门新技术等等，明确了目的，清楚了任务，你自然能从噪音中筛选出有用的信息。
en: For example, reading, talking heart-to-heart with friends, learning a new technology, etc. Once the purpose is clear and the task is clear, you can naturally filter useful information from the noise.

text: 学生时代的学霸通常就能做到这一点。
en: Top students in their student days can usually do this.

text: 和那些成天开小差的人相比，学霸接触到的噪音其实并不比他们少，但学霸的专注程度，绝对是那些学渣们所望尘莫及的。
en: Compared with those who daydream all day, top students actually come into contact with no less noise, but their level of focus is absolutely beyond the reach of underachieving students.

text: 因为他们早已意识到，把学校教的知识学到手，成绩排名提高到第一第二，才是应试教育下最应该做的事情，否则就会在终极一考的比赛中被分配到资源匮乏的地方。
en: Because they have long realised that mastering the knowledge taught in school and raising their grade ranking to first or second is the most important thing under exam-oriented education; otherwise, they will be assigned to resource-poor places in the ultimate exam competition.

text: 当然，这并不是教你去做一个无趣的人。
en: Of course, this is not teaching you to be a boring person.

text: 不过多数时候，我们也会发现，过分关注那些与我们并不相关的信息，其实并不见得能够让我们更有趣，生活更好，反而分散了注意力，徒增了各种嘈杂情绪。
en: But most of the time, we also find that excessively paying attention to information irrelevant to us does not necessarily make us more interesting or life better; instead, it disperses attention and adds various noisy emotions.
